messages:
Alex: Heads-up — gitops reconcile in eu-gpu started failing ~10m ago. Helm hooks are spinning on a terraform apply step because the remote state key was rotated in the backend yesterday and some CI runners still use the old key prefix.
Priya: ugh, which repo? any errors in the reconcile log?
Alex: infra/cluster-provisioner. Reconcile log shows terraform failing to acquire lock. Snippet:
```
2024-12-10T09:12:03Z error: Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed
 status: BadRequest
```
Alex: The s3 key prefix was moved from `state/eu/legacy/` -> `state/eu/v2/` as part of the last migration. Most pipelines were updated but a small fraction of ephemeral CI images still init with the old backend key.
Jamal: That explains the race — old runner tries to init with old key, cannot find expected lock entry in Dynamo and then create fails? We saw similar when workspace aliases were changed.
SRE Oncall: Before we force anything — are there any in-flight applies that have actually created resources? We should avoid force-unlock if a real apply is midflight.
Alex: Checked tasks; no active long-running println applies in the cluster. Last successful apply timestamp in metrics is 2 hours ago. Looks like the agents got stuck at `terraform init`/`terraform plan` step.
Priya: Quick mitigation: update arg to the gitops helm chart so the pre-sync job sets the correct backend key via env var. Then restart reconcile. But we need a durable fix so this doesn't recur on state-key rotations.
Jamal: Agreed. Also propose adding a short leader-election step for GitOps pre-sync hooks: one pod obtains a transient lock (k8s ConfigMap annotation) before running terraform, so concurrent reconcile workers in the same cluster don't race on backend changes.
Alex: I'm going to force-unlock the orphaned dynamo entry if it's safe. Command to inspect current locks:
```bash
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tfstate-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"/state/eu/v2/cluster-provisioner.tfstate"}}'
```
If the item has TTL expired and no holder, we can run:
```bash
terraform force-unlock -force <LOCK_ID>
```
Priya: Add a postmortem checklist item: when rotating state keys, create a small migration job that updates CI images/helm charts and then pauses reconcilers for a minute. Maybe a feature flag to opt-in so we can coordinate.
SRE Oncall: +1. Also we should surface the backend-key mismatch as a clearer alert (currently just a generic lock failure). Tagging ops-alerts.
infra-bot: deploybot: rollout started for infra/helm-chart: gitops-backend-fix -> canary (1/3). Logs will stream to /deploys/1742.
Alex: I'll open a PR (infra#3422) that: (1) patches the helm pre-sync to read backend key mapping from a configmap (2) adds a leader-election sidecar for pre-sync jobs (3) adds a migration job template for state-prefix rotations.
Jamal: For immediate relief, I manually restarted the stuck reconcile pod in eu-gpu and bumped the env var to new key; reconcile resumed and completed. No force-unlock needed.
Priya: Sweet. Post-incident follow-ups: update CI images, add docs to runbook for state-key migrations, add an automated smoke test that runs `terraform init` with both old and new key to catch stale images.
Alex: Thanks all. I'll land the PR and schedule a quick playbook doc. If anyone sees the old key show up again, ping me directly.
SRE Oncall: Marking incident as "triaged" for now. Will watch the next 2 reconciles for flakiness.
